name: Workshop Preparation
obj: Translate Define outputs into a workshop with the right activities, sequence, materials and roles.
who: Lead facilitator designs · Co-facilitators own groups · Client sponsor confirms objectives and participants.
when: 2-3 weeks before the workshop; groups (05.05) set before the day.
inputs: Personas, journey, HMW, concept sheets, participant list. Minimum: one stated outcome per activity.
output: Workshop Facilitation Pack: agenda, run-of-show, roles, canvases, prompts, timing, logistics, expected outputs.
std: Agenda adds up to the slot (Format A = 240 min, Format B = 480 min); every activity has an output; plan B exists.
quality: Purposeful activities; balance of divergence and convergence; clear roles; contingency.
mistakes: Planning activities instead of outcomes · no buffer · no dry run.
example: WORK: Northbridge Format A half-day — outcome: improved future lunch journey + 6 idea sheets + owners. [fictional]

var.PLAY: Format B full day at the stadium with stewards.
var.HEAL: Format A on ward time; nurses join for 60 minutes only.
var.LEARN: Format A with students; evening slot.

prompt: 'Design a Format A (09:00-13:00) run-of-show for [objective] with [participants]. Each activity: purpose, output, timing, facilitator role, plan B.'
verify: Timing sums; feasibility with real participants; accessibility.
fallback: Copy the Format A / B agenda on the Start Here frame and adapt.
l_obj: Commit to an outcome and sequence activities that produce it, with a plan B.

templates.label: Project template root (SharePoint) — specific template: TO LOCATE, owner Gabriel

exercise.situation: Three hours, sixteen participants, a client who wants 'lots of ideas'.
questions: What outcome would you commit to instead?
Sketch the sequence and what each step produces.
Plan B if only half show up?

answer_key.sample_answer: Outcome: 6-8 developed idea sheets on 2 priority moments, with owners. Plan B: merge groups, keep personas, cut one ideation round.
answer_key.success_criteria: Each activity names its output; plan B keeps the outcome.

name: Ice Breaker — Facilitation
obj: Run the opening activity so everyone contributes and moves into co-creation mode.
who: Facilitator runs it · Co-facilitators model participation.
output: An activated group where everyone has spoken.
std: Every participant contributed at least once; time kept.
mistakes: Letting one senior voice dominate · overrunning · no link to the challenge.
example: HEAL: 'A meal someone cared about' — silent writing 2 min, then round-robin; facilitator links stories to Ruth's journey.
prompt: Generic Claude prompt (prep only): 'Give me 3 facilitation moves if one senior person dominates the ice breaker.'
l_obj: Use silent-first and round-robin techniques to balance voices.
explain: The ice breaker should activate the behaviours you need for the rest of the workshop.

templates.label: Project template root (SharePoint) — specific template: TO LOCATE, owner Gabriel

exercise.situation: Two participants stay silent while a senior director answers everything.
questions: What do you do in the moment?
Which instruction would have prevented it?
How do you close so energy carries on?

answer_key.sample_answer: Thank, then go round the room; ask the director to listen first. Prevent with silent writing. Close by naming the patterns heard.
answer_key.success_criteria: Intervention is respectful and restores balance.

name: Workshop PowerPoint
obj: Build a clear deck that guides participants through context, activities, timing and transitions.
who: CoDesign team builds · Facilitator rehearses with it.
output: Workshop deck: welcome, context, objectives, agenda, insights, instructions, inspiration, transitions, recap, next steps.
std: Each activity slide lets a group start without asking: task, time, output, materials.
quality: Simple, visual, one purpose per slide.
mistakes: 45 slides for 3 hours · instructions only spoken · insights repeated from pre-read in full.
handoff: Deck used live; final version filed with 06.01.
example: LEARN: 18 slides for a half-day; activity slides show 'Task / Time / Output / Where'.
prompt: Generic Claude prompt: 'Turn this run-of-show into a slide list: one slide per activity with Task, Time, Output, Materials.'
l_obj: Cut a deck to the slides that move the workshop forward and write a self-explanatory activity slide.
explain: The PowerPoint is not the workshop. It is its navigation system.

exercise.situation: Your deck has 45 slides for a three-hour workshop.
questions: Which slides do you keep, and why?
What must an activity slide contain?
What belongs on the wall instead?

answer_key.sample_answer: Keep welcome, objective, agenda, 1 insight per activity, activity slides, recap. Activity slide = task, time, output, materials. Personas and journey belong on the wall.

name: CoCreation Journey Map / Future Journey
obj: Use the current journey as a canvas to imagine and structure a better end-to-end experience.
who: Facilitator guides · Participants ideate and position ideas · CoDesign team captures.
when: Core workshop activity, after evidence immersion.
output: Future Journey Map with ideas, improved touchpoints, new services and priority directions.
std: Shows what changes, where, and why, versus the current journey.
quality: Linked to real needs; end-to-end; exploratory.
mistakes: Jumping to an app · ideas floating off the journey · no current/future contrast.
example: WORK: under 'Lunch', ideas 'team table' and 'pre-order by 11:00' replace the two-queue pain; 'Find a place' gets 'quiet hours zone'.

var.HEAL: Ordering moves to same day; family update added.

prompt: After the session: 'Cluster these future-journey stickies [paste] by stage and theme; flag duplicates; do not add new ideas.'
fallback: Facilitator clusters live on the wall.
l_obj: Bring a solution-first group back to the journey and show current-vs-future difference.
explain: Don't ideate in isolation. Design the experience as a journey.

exercise.situation: A group starts inventing a mobile app before looking at the journey.
questions: How do you bring them back?
Where should their idea sit, and what changes?
How do you show current vs future?

answer_key.sample_answer: Ask 'which moment does this fix, for whom?'. Place it on the stage; write the before/after on two colours.
answer_key.success_criteria: Idea anchored to a stage and a need.

name: Participants & Group Separation
obj: Create balanced groups mixing perspectives, expertise and seniority. Set up before the workshop day.
who: Lead facilitator composes · Client sponsor confirms the list.
when: 2 days to 1 week before; it is an input to 05.01 even though it is taught after 05.04.
inputs: Participant list with role, function, seniority, user proximity.
output: Group setup: allocation, challenge or persona, facilitator per group.
std: Every group has at least one end user or user-proximate person; no function dominates.
mistakes: Grouping by department · director in every group · no end user.
example: HEAL: 3 groups of 5, each with a nurse or ward host, a dietitian or kitchen lead, a family representative; the director floats as 'challenger' in the share-back.

var.WORK: Mix team leads and occasional attendees.

prompt: Generic Claude prompt: 'Allocate these 15 participants [table] into 3 balanced groups by function, seniority and user proximity; explain trade-offs.'
verify: Interpersonal dynamics the AI cannot know.
fallback: Sort cards by function, deal them round-robin, then swap for balance.
l_obj: Compose groups with an explicit logic and place senior people deliberately.
explain: Group people to create complementary perspectives, not by function.

templates.label: Project template root (SharePoint) — specific template: TO LOCATE, owner Gabriel

exercise.situation: List received 2 days before: 4 managers, 3 dietitians, 5 employees, 2 IT, 1 director.
questions: How do you build groups, on which logic?
Where does the director go, and why?
What if a group has no end user?

answer_key.sample_answer: 3 groups of 5 mixing roles; director as share-back challenger or in a group with a strong facilitator; swap an employee in, or give that group user evidence cards.
answer_key.success_criteria: Logic explicit; every group has user voice.

name: Give Inspiration — AI Ideas
obj: Use AI as a creative stimulus to widen and challenge ideas, after humans have ideated first.
who: Facilitator prepares and introduces stimuli · Participants react, challenge, remix.
acc: Lead facilitator; approved AI use only.
when: After a first human ideation round, when a group is stuck or converging too early.
inputs: Persona, moment, need, HMW, existing ideas, constraints.
output: AI inspiration prompts and directions, selected and enriched by participants.
std: AI ideas labelled as AI; participants decide what stays.
mistakes: Showing AI ideas first · presenting them as answers · unapproved tools.
example: PLAY: group stuck on half-time; facilitator shows 5 AI directions incl. 'reverse the queue: food comes to the seat'; the group remixes it into section lockers. AI inspiration is a creative stimulus, not evidence.

var.HEAL: AI directions screened for clinical safety first.

prompt: 'Persona [x] at moment [y] needs [z]. HMW [q]. Existing ideas: [list]. Constraints: [list]. Give 8 directions that are different from the existing ideas, 2 deliberately provocative. One line each.'
verify: Remove unsafe or off-brief ideas before showing; label as AI.
l_obj: Brief an AI with useful context and present its output without shutting down the group.
explain: Human first. AI second. Human decides.

templates.label: Project template root (SharePoint) — specific template: TO LOCATE, owner Gabriel

exercise.situation: A group is stuck after twenty minutes of ideation.
questions: What do you give the AI so the output is useful?
How do you present AI ideas without shutting down thinking?
What do you do with a brilliant but infeasible idea?

answer_key.sample_answer: Persona, moment, need, constraints, existing ideas. Present as 'provocations to react to'. Keep the principle, park the feature.
answer_key.success_criteria: Prompt includes constraints and existing ideas.

name: Idea Sheet
obj: Turn promising workshop ideas into clear sheets that can be compared, combined and prioritised.
when: End of ideation in the workshop.
output: Completed Idea Sheets ready to compare and prioritise.
std: Readable in 30 seconds; need and HMW filled.
quality: Simple, visual, connected to a need, open.
mistakes: 'Better communication' as an idea · finished solutions · no user value.
handoff: Idea Sheets capture participants' contributions → 06.01 Summary and 06.02 Prioritisation. Selected ideas are strengthened later in 06.X1.
example: LEARN: 'Gap Base' — commuters book a study pod with a meal bundle; need: a place for the 3-hour gap. [fictional]
prompt: After the workshop only: 'Transcribe these idea sheet photos [attach] into a table; keep participants' words; flag missing fields.'
l_obj: Coach a group from a vague idea to a one-line description linked to a need.
explain: Make the idea tangible enough to discuss, not so finished that it cannot change.

templates.label: Project template root (SharePoint) — specific template: TO LOCATE, owner Gabriel

questions: What do you ask to make it tangible?
Write the one-line description and the need.
What stays open?

answer_key.sample_answer: 'Who, about what, at which moment?' → 'Text families when the patient has eaten' / need: reassurance. Open: channel, privacy rules.
